Utilities for processing d-style string formatting specifications (eg "xx.dx")

Source: R/jjcsformats_d.R, R/zzz_format_d_setup.R
fmt_spec_d.Rd

Usage

fmt_spec_single_d(
  d = 1,
  stats_in = NULL,
  fmt_d_def = junco_def_d_all,
  fmt_d_in = NULL
)

fmt_spec_df_d(
  df_d,
  d_column = "d",
  fmt_column = "fmt_d",
  stats_in = NULL,
  fmt_d_def = junco_def_d_all,
  fmt_d_in = NULL
)

fmt_spec_var_d(
  var_d,
  stats_in = NULL,
  fmt_d_def = junco_def_d_all,
  fmt_d_in = NULL
)

junco_def_d_all

junco_def_d_alt1

junco_def_d_alt2

Format

  • junco_def_d_all Used as default input vector for argument fmt_d_def in functions fmt_spec_single_d(), fmt_spec_df_d() and fmt_spec_var_d() (corresponds to the named vector of with default available formats junco_default_formats with d = 1)

  • junco_def_d_alt1 Alternative vector of d-style specification defaults.

  • junco_def_d_alt2 Another alternative vector of d-style specification defaults.

Arguments

d

integer(1) Value of d for the translation of "xx.dx" into "xx.xx" style (example when d = 1)

stats_in

(character) Set of statistics to restrict to.

fmt_d_def

Named vector with default format specifications where d-style format is allowed.

fmt_d_in

Named vector with format specifications where d-style format is allowed. Formats defined here will take higher precedence over formats in fmt_d_def.

df_d

Dataframe in which the d-column specification is available.

d_column

Name of column within dataframe df_d that contains required integer values for d.

fmt_column

Name of column that will be added to dataframe that will contain resulting format specifications.

var_d

Named vector of d specifications. Names are to be considered as variables to be analyzed in further processing.

Details

Format specifications in d-style notation (such as "xx.dx") will be translated to string based formats (or wrapped with jjcsformat_xx()), eg "xx.dx" will be translated into "xx.xx", when d = 1.

Functions

  • fmt_spec_single_d(): Function to convert a named list using d-style string format specification into a named list with valid formatters formatting specification

  • fmt_spec_df_d(): Function to convert an input column with d-style formatting specification into a new column with valid formatters formatting specification.

    The new column can be passed onto argument formats_var in rtables::analyze() function.

  • fmt_spec_var_d(): Function to convert a named list of variables with d-style formatting specification into a named list with valid formatters formatting specification.

    The result can be used as input for argument format in rtables::analyze() call.

  • junco_def_d_all: Named vector of default format specification using d-style notation.

  • junco_def_d_alt1: Alternative vector of d-style specification defaults.

  • junco_def_d_alt2: Another alternative vector of d-style specification defaults.

Examples

junco_def_d <- c(
  "mean" = "xx.dx",
  "mean_sd" = "xx.dx (xx.dxx)",
  "mean_se" = "xx.dx (xx.dxx)",
  "range" = "(xx.d, xx.d)"
)
myfmts <- fmt_spec_single_d(
  d = 1,
  stats_in = c("mean", "mean_sd"),
  fmt_d_def = junco_def_d,
  fmt_d_in = NULL
)
myfmts
#> $mean
#> [1] "xx.xx"
#> 
#> $mean_sd
#> [1] "xx.xx (xx.xxx)"
#> 

# example for fmt_spec_df_d ----
library(dplyr)
df_d <- tribble(
  ~PARAMCD, ~d,
  "DIABP", 2L,
  "PULSE", 3L,
  "RESP", 1L
)
yy <- fmt_spec_df_d(df_d,
  d_column = "d",
  fmt_column = "fmt_d",
  stats_in = NULL,
  fmt_d_def = junco_def_d,
  fmt_d_in = NULL
)


df <- ex_advs |>
  filter(PARAMCD %in% c("DIABP", "PULSE", "RESP")) |>
  filter(AVISIT %in% c("BASELINE", "WEEK 1 DAY 8", "WEEK 2 DAY 15"))
df <- df |>
  left_join(yy)
#> Joining with `by = join_by(PARAMCD)`

lyt <- basic_table() |>
  split_cols_by("ARMCD") |>
  split_rows_by("PARAMCD", split_fun = drop_split_levels) |>
  split_rows_by("AVISIT", split_fun = drop_split_levels) |>
  analyze(
    vars = "AVAL",
    afun = tern::a_summary,
    extra_args = list(
      .stats = c("n", "mean_se", "range"),
      .formats = "default"
    ),
    formats_var = "fmt_d"
  )

rslt <- build_table(lyt, df, alt_counts_df = ex_adsl)
rslt

# example for fmt_spec_var_d ----
var <- c("AGE" = 0, "BMI" = 1, "BMRKR1" = 2)
vars_fmt <- fmt_spec_var_d(var,
  stats_in = NULL,
  fmt_d_def = junco_def_d,
  fmt_d_in = NULL
)
vars_fmt

lyt <- basic_table() |>
  split_cols_by("ARMCD") |>
  analyze(
    vars = c("AGE", "BMRKR1"),
    afun = tern::a_summary,
    extra_args = list(
      .stats = c("n", "mean_sd", "range"),
      .formats = "default"
    ),
    format = vars_fmt,
    section_div = " "
  )

rslt <- build_table(lyt, ex_adsl)
rslt
